paragraphs: Rabbi Acha, son of Rav Huna, Berakhot 32a.

notes.text: The frozen middle notice begins רק אחא, literally “only Acha.” The consulted Berakhot32a explicitly has Rav Acha son of Rav Huna. Rav is bracketed as the proposed reading; the source letters remain unchanged.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 336) has ר׳ אחא, “Rabbi Acha,” where the supplied text has רק אחא. The consulted Berakhot 32a says “Rav Acha son of Rav Huna,” and Berakhot 34b says “Rav Chiyya son of Rav Huna.” The earlier translation bracketed “Rav” on the strength of Berakhot 32a. The consulted Shabbat 66b records Avin bar Huna without a title in the selected statements. The three notices do not establish that all three men had the same father.
